corrected_draft.description_long: On February 25, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a memorandum to the Secretaries of State, Defense, Energy and the Attorney General, and to the directors of OMB, National Intelligence, CIA and OPM. It also directed agencies to terminate Covington engagements to the maximum extent permitted by law, required OPM to forward the memorandum to other clearance-granting agencies as needed, and instructed OMB to issue guidance for reviewing all government contracts with the firm. The memorandum stated that agencies should align funding decisions with administration priorities to the extent permitted by law. The White House’s published text establishes these directives; it does not establish that a review found misconduct or that every clearance or contract was actually terminated. GovInfo republishes the text but notes that an original was unavailable to it for verification. The held entry’s March 14 executive-order date and instrument are therefore inaccurate; this was a February 25 presidential memorandum.

corrected_draft.description_long: An Associated Press report published April 18, 2017, said Ivanka Trump’s company received provisional approval from China on April 6 for three trademarks covering jewelry, bags and spa services. That evening, Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner attended a Mar-a-Lago dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife. The report distinguished the three approvals announced for that date from the wider trademark portfolio: it said the company then had 16 registered trademarks in China and 32 pending applications, and that four marks had received preliminary approval since the inauguration. Thus, “16” described registered marks overall, not the number newly approved on April 6. The article also discussed the family’s stated ethics safeguards and concerns raised by former government ethics officials about business and policy overlap. This draft reports the discrete trademark approval and dinner chronology, without treating the timing as proof of improper influence or asserting that all 16 marks were granted that day.
